name: Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport
before:
Arizona's largest airport, only three miles east of downtown Phoenix, and eleventh busiest in the United States. It is a hub for American Airlines and a base for Southwest and Frontier.

The terminal numbering catches everyone out. There are only two terminals and they are called 3 and 4. Terminals 1 and 2 were retired and the airport chose not to renumber the survivors because passengers already knew them. Terminal 4 is the big one with 92 gates, used by American, Southwest and all international carriers. Terminal 3 has 27 gates and takes most other domestic and pre-cleared arrivals, including Alaska, Delta, United and Frontier.

Three parallel runways serve the 3,400 acre site, all of them able to take aircraft at 900,000 lb or more.

It is a joint civil and military field. The 161st Air Refueling Wing of the Arizona Air National Guard flies KC-135R tankers from the Goldwater enclave here, so military aircraft are routine.
after:
Arizona's largest airport, east of downtown Phoenix. It handled 51.6 million passengers in 2025 and is a hub for American Airlines.

The terminal numbering catches people out: there are only two terminals, numbered 3 and 4. Terminal 4 is the big one, used by American, Southwest and most international airlines, including British Airways, which has flown nonstop to London since 1996. Most other domestic flights and pre-cleared arrivals use Terminal 3, including Alaska, Delta, United and Frontier. Sky Harbor says a new six-gate North Concourse at Terminal 3 should be finished in 2027.

Three runways serve the 3,400 acre site.

It is a joint civil and military field. The 161st Air Refueling Wing, part of the Arizona Air National Guard, flies KC-135R tankers from Goldwater Air National Guard Base here.

claims.note: Was 'only three miles east'. The coordinates give 4.0 miles in a straight line from the GeoNames centre, so three miles is a ratio of 0.75 and fails the check. The FAA master record says '03 E', which is three NAUTICAL miles (about 3.5 statute miles), while Wikipedia gives 3 statute miles and converts it to 2.6 nautical miles, so the written sources do not agree on the figure; the operator's pages give no distance. The bearing is agreed by all three.

claims.wasBefore: only three miles east of downtown Phoenix
claims.why: Fails the coordinates check (4.0 miles in a straight line, ratio 0.75); the FAA gives 3 nautical miles and Wikipedia 3 statute miles, and the operator gives no figure. The bearing is kept.

claims.claim: eleventh busiest in the United States
claims.wasBefore: and eleventh busiest in the United States
claims.why: Good sources disagree: Wikipedia says 11th by boardings in 2025, but the FAA's preliminary CY2025 table ranks Phoenix 13th (25,094,817), behind Charlotte and Seattle. Replaced by the operator's 2025 passenger total.

claims.claim: a base for Southwest and Frontier
claims.wasBefore: and a base for Southwest and Frontier
claims.why: Rests on Wikipedia alone: Southwest's media fact sheets page had nothing on it and no Frontier source was found. Southwest stays in the text through its terminal.

claims.claim: numbering catches everyone out; called 3 and 4
claims.wasBefore: The terminal numbering catches everyone out. There are only two terminals and they are called 3 and 4.

claims.claim: Terminals 1 and 2 retired; airport chose not to renumber
claims.wasBefore: Terminals 1 and 2 were retired and the airport chose not to renumber the survivors because passengers already knew them.
claims.why: Only Wikipedia gives the reason; none of the operator's pages read (airlines, about, history, development, maps, parking FAQ) explains the numbering.

claims.wasBefore: Terminal 4 is the big one with 92 gates, used by American, Southwest and all international carriers.
claims.why: The gate count rests on Wikipedia alone (which also says '86 (now 92)' and 119 in all); 'all international carriers' is wrong on the operator's list, which puts Air Canada and Porter in Terminal 3.

claims.wasBefore: Terminal 3 has 27 gates and takes most other domestic and pre-cleared arrivals
claims.why: The gate count rests on Wikipedia alone, and six more gates are being added (operator, August 2026). The allocation is kept.

claims.wasBefore: Three parallel runways serve the 3,400 acre site, all of them able to take aircraft at 900,000 lb or more.
claims.why: 'Parallel' and the weight limit rest on Wikipedia alone: the FAA record lists the runways as 07L/25R, 07R/25L and 08/26 and its weight fields did not come through in the saved text. Three runways and the site area are kept.

claims.claim: the Goldwater enclave; military aircraft routine
claims.wasBefore: from the Goldwater enclave here, so military aircraft are routine
claims.why: The base is now named as its wing names it; 'routine' is a judgement (the operator's 2025 figures show 1,194 military movements at Sky Harbor, down from 2,271 in 2024).

opinion.text: The terminal numbering catches people out
opinion.why: The old text's framing, softened from 'everyone'; the numbering it points to is sourced above.
